newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends with pared losses after new lows.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends with pared losses after new lows.

text.p: London cocoa futures ended with pared losses on light manufacturer interest after persistent selling drove the March contract to a new session low of 911 stg.
The market took a sharp downward move after its recent losses were said to have disappointed longs and drove industry buyers further away.
There was also a little bit of follow-through selling from New York in early afternoon, traders said.

"But after a while the market became heavily oversold technically, especially in New York, and was due for a bounce," said a trader. New York prices were helped at one stage by spec buying and trade and industry
"We've been following New York rather than the other way around. London saw mixed buying and selling," said one.
By the close, benchmark March stood nine stg down at 916 stg a tonne after dipping to a session low of 911 and just above the key 910 support.
"I suspect there was a bit of manufacturing interest in London. But real interest may begin if we pop down to 900," another trader said.
March has been sliding since Tuesday in persistent sales said to have included a cocktail of fund liquidation and short selling.
Volume was 7,944 lots comprising mainly crosses and AAs.
On the switches, Dec/March traded at a stable 33 stg.
"There is nothing to buck the trend," said one trader commenting on the market's increased downside momentum.
Traders were frustrated by stubbornly narrow daily price ranges and lack of outright turnover.
Analysts said the contract could drift to 880 stg along a downtrend channel in place since October, but mild support could be expected at around 910 stg.
Susan Rigg of Chart Analysis reckoned the downside could be limited in short-term and March would soon look to form a base.
Tuesday's sales resulted in a massive drop of 4,266 lots in December uncovered positions which could be interpreted as long liquidation. The uncovered position is now 12,998.
Trade remained slow in the physical cocoa market with industry believed to be covered for the first quarter of 1997.
A Dutch buyer was said to have quoted 45 stg under (London futures) for February shipment of Ivorian cocoa -- a level traders said was "incredibly cheap".
